Same A-Class Motorhome, Different Clothes: The 2027 Pilote G740FGJ Evidence Goes for Bold
8 photos
Photo: Pilote
You can't put lipstick on a pig, but you CAN take a product that's already appreciated for its features, comfort, and style and turn it into something even better by giving it a new set of "clothes." That's what Pilote is doing with the Galaxy A-Class motorhome series for 2027.
Like many other European RV specialists, Pilote is also going for an upgraded style for the 2027 model year, but the difference is that, in their case, the upgrade is more than aesthetic and actually results in more interior volume. With any RV, but particularly with the more compact ones, any increase in interior volume means more comfort and more functionality, so it's a win for the end customer.
Of the series of motorhomes produced by the French Pilote, the Galaxy is the higher-end offer in their catalog. The Galaxy series is the series of high-end integrated A-Class motorhomes, offered in two configurations, Expression and Evidence, one being the basic version and the other the "all-inclusive" equivalent.
Today, we're looking at the Pilote G740FGJ in the Evidence spec. Of the 17 floorplans available in the entire Galaxy series for 2027, this one is among the largest and most luxurious, so it's a perfect example of what Pilote understands by luxury RV-ing in a still relatively compact form factor.
Photo: Pilote Unlike what you will find in other territories (U.S., here's looking at you!), that means a yacht-like, very elegant interior, double floor construction with plenty of storage options, two separate sleeping spaces with some spatial and physical separation for privacy, and the basics in terms of creature comforts. It also means a relative compact form factor but with an interior design that does away with the feeling of being crammed in like sardines.
This floorplan debuted in 2021, but you would probably not recognize an older model as the same one that Pilote brought out at several trade shows in the fall of 2026, to present changes for the 2027 model year. The 2027 G740FGJ debuts with a brand-new face, a brand new rear, a completely redesigned interior, and the most important part, more body length.
It's not just nicer to look at , if your idea of "nice" is a square, aggressive, and arguably futuristic front end, but longer by almost 10 cm (4 inches). The 2027 model is on a Fiat CCS chassis offered standard with a 2.2-liter engine with 180 hp and an automatic transmission, and it comes in at 7.56 meters (24.8 feet) of total length.
Photo: Pilote That Fiat chassis is the 4.5-ton one, so you're looking at a maximum permissible weight of 4,250 kg (9,369 lbs) with 1,054 kg (2,323 lbs) of payload. It could still be called "lightweight" if you compare it to much larger RVs, but it can't be operated on a standard B Category driving license.
This is a 4-bed motorhome, with 4 belted seats and 5 or 6 seats around the dining table. The layout remains essentially unchanged from previous years, and it's definitely not anything you haven't seen before if you're familiar with European or Euro-style motorhomes , but the interior overhaul adds an extra note of sophistication to it. It's not super-fancy or pretentious in an annoying way, so truly elegant.
You have a front lounge slash dining area at the front, with two large face-to-face benches and the swivel captain chairs. Over the dinette is the first sleeping area, in the form of a drop-down bed that tucks discreetly, though not invisibly, into the ceiling over the cab area.
Photo: Pilote The kitchen is next, with a new large hybrid compression fridge on the campside (also a novelty for 2027) and a compact galley that feels more elevated than it needs to be. That's not a bad thing; when you have little space to work with, it helps that it looks good.
The galley comes standard with a two-burner gas cooktop and a separate sink under a glass cover, and dedicated storage under and above the counter. Accent lighting, an accent wall, and a new blacksplash that matches the black hardware help elevate this (compact) space.
The second sleeping area is at the rear, in the form of twin beds you can join into a full king by using the slatted extension and the inserts provided. These beds have overhead storage and large wardrobes underneath; they also sit on top of the huge pass-through garage that offers 116 cm (45.6 inches) of headroom, so it's perfect for hauling bigger, bulkier, and taller items.
Photo: Pilote That same garage comes fully stocked, at least by European standards. That means you get shelves and cubbies, lights, an outdoor shower, and a pair of rails to which you can secure your bikes or even one of those larger sitting scooters. Non-slip flooring is included as well.
The bathroom inside is a pass-through one, with a large shower on one side and the washroom across from it. You can use each space separately or join them into a single room, with space left to change clothes. Alternatively, you can close off the bathroom to have privacy in the bedroom.
The 2027 Pilote G740FGJ comes with the full Evidence package (black awning, rearview camera, electric step), a 6,000W Truma Combi D6E space heater and water heater, a 200Ah lithium battery and a 210W monocrystalline solar panel, a smaller gas bottle, a TV mount in the living room, and 130 liters (34 gallons) for freshwater and 95 liters (25 gallons) for gray. The wastewater tank is heated.
Photo: Pilote Pilote calls the Pilote G740FGJ in the Evidence configuration "comfort without compromise," now with an instantly recognizable exterior design. This kind of no-compromise RV life will cost you upwards of €97,790 ($109,200 at the current exchange rate), which is the starting price for the 2027 model before options.
